From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Cc: network_ops@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:05:37 -0700
Subject: Re: [BrightCart] Sudden 5xx/timeout spike — checkout failures impacting >10%

Team / Alex — quick technical summary from SRE:
- At ~07:58 PT we observed a set of DNS resolution failures for several brightcart.* hostnames in our edge POPs. Upstream resolver chains returned SERVFAIL/NXDOMAIN intermittently; these failures cascaded into connection setup timeouts and then to our application layer retries.
- Retry amplification: multiple clients retried aggressively (exponential backoff not respected), leading to queueing and 503s from our upstream ELBs.
- Impacted paths: checkout API (/v1/checkout/submit), cart validation, and attribution pixel endpoints.

Immediate mitigations applied:
1) Reduced retry window on our edge proxies for BrightCart routes to limit amplification.
2) Temporarily disabled aggressive HTTP/1 keepalive reuse on five POPs showing the worst DNS latencies.
3) Added short-term caching (TTL=30s) for brightcart DNS answers at our resolver layer when we see successive SERVFAIL to reduce downstream queries.

Action items:
- We are contacting CloudEdge (DNS provider) and AWS support to trace whether there was a DNS configuration push or resolver outage.
- Request BrightCart to confirm whether they pushed any DNS changes or CloudEdge configuration updates around 07:50-08:05 PT.
- If CloudEdge confirms config push, we will coordinate rollback/soft-fix and clear TTLs.

I'll post SRE traces and sample request-ids once sanitized.

-Rishi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Cc: markus_klein@redwood.ai

Subject: Post-incident status: DNS propagation cascade identified — mitigation complete

Alex / team — final update for today.

Root cause (summary): CloudEdge rolled an automated configuration deployment that, for a small subset of customers (including BrightCart), briefly altered resolution behavior for delegated hostnames. This produced intermittent SERVFAIL/NXDOMAIN responses across multiple public resolvers. The intermittent failures triggered client-side retry amplification which exhausted backend capacity and produced increased 5xx/429 rates at our ELBs.

What we did:
- Applied short TTL caching at our resolver layer to absorb noisy upstream failures (TTL=30s) and prevented requery storms.
- Rate-limited retries at proxy layer for BrightCart routes.
- Coordinated with BrightCart and CloudEdge; CloudEdge reverted the problematic deployment at ~12:05 PT. Post-reversion monitoring shows normalized DNS resolution and a steady drop in 5xx rates.
- Opened a joint RCA with CloudEdge and BrightCart engineers (Jira SUP-1123).

Current status: mitigations in place; error rates returned to baseline by ~15:30 PT. No further customer-facing action required right now.

Next steps / action items:
- Postmortem owner: rishi_malhotra to coordinate final RCA (deliverable: EOD next business day).
- Finance & Account: monica_patel to propose service credit options to BrightCart (reference DEAL-3487).
- Engineering: implement resolver-level circuit-breaker logic to avoid cache thrash on intermittent SERVFAIL within 48 hours.

Attachments included in this thread: cloudwatch_spike.png, dns_traceroute.zip, brightcart_request_log_snippet.txt

Monica
